## Why Regularization?

- The **additive** linear models (Linear, Logistic, GLM) can be limiting by assuming a line.
  - However, these models tend to perform better, and more efficiently than other models.
  - They also allow for inferential procedures.
- Regularization will improve prediction accuracy and model interpretability.



::: {.callout-caution}

Statisticians warn against using regularization techniques as it threatens inference. If one must be done, Ridge Regression is preferred.

:::


# Regularization

## Regularization

Shrinkage methods are techniques that will reduce a full parameterized model (a high number of predictors) to a lower parameterized model (a smaller number of predictors).

## Ridge Regression

Ridge regression incorporates a shrinkage penalty term to the least squares formula. The shrinkage penalty term will reduce the $\beta$ coefficients towards 0 based on a penalty parameter ($\lambda$)

## Ridge Regression

$$\sum^n_{i=1}\left(Y_i-\beta_0 +\sum^p_{j=1}X_{ij}\beta_j\right)^2 + \lambda\sum^p_{j=1}\beta_j^2$$

## Ridge Regression

$$
\ell(\boldsymbol \beta|\boldsymbol Y;\boldsymbol X) = \sum^n_{i=1}\log\left(f\left\{Y_i;\boldsymbol \beta, X_i\right\}\right) + \lambda\sum^p_{j=1}\beta_j^2
$$

## Why does Ridge Regression Work?

The inclusion of a tuning parameter $\lambda$ helps control the bias-variance tradeoff. An increase in $\lambda$ will begin to reduce the variance, while slightly increasing the bias in the prediction of new data.    


## LASSO

Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) is known as a shrinkage method which forces $\beta$ coefficients that do not have a significant predict power towards and possibly equal to 0.

## LASSO

$$\sum^n_{i=1}\left(Y_i-\beta_0 +\sum^p_{j=1}X_{ij}\beta_j\right)^2 + \lambda\sum^p_{j=1}|\beta_j|$$

## LASSO

$$
\ell(\boldsymbol \beta|\boldsymbol Y;\boldsymbol X) = \sum^n_{i=1}\log\left(f\left\{Y_i;\boldsymbol \beta, X_i\right\}\right) + + \lambda\sum^p_{j=1}|\beta_j|
$$


## Why Ridge or LASSO?

Each method is capable on identifying the optimum MSE for the Bias-Variance trade-off scenario. This will lead to a lower prediction error. The key is to find the optimal penalty parameter. This can be done with a Cross-Validation technique (next lecture).
